title: Apply for a fireworks (single use) licence
summary: This page provides information on how to apply for a fireworks (single use) licence (FSUL) to legally purchase, possess, use, store, and transport fireworks for a single event.
intro:
A fireworks (single use) licence (FSUL) allows you to purchase, possess, use, store and transport fireworks.

The licence is only valid for the single event that you nominate in your application, and you're only permitted to hold the type and quantity of fireworks for no more than 5 working days prior to the display.

You can apply for up to 4 FSULs in any 12 months.

If you want to use fireworks often, or include aerial shell type fireworks in your displays, you'll need to apply for a pyrotechnician's licence.
who_can_apply: Have successfully completed training/instruction given by a person with a current pyrotechnician’s licence in the safe use of the fireworks to be used for the event or display.
Only use the fireworks for an organised public event.
If less than seven working days notice is given to Safework NSW or for an extended display, a supporting letter from the local Council stating they have no objections is required.
Be able to demonstrate that you have notified the police, fire brigades, local council, and any other relevant agencies.
what_you_need: Confirmation that you have completed the fireworks display checklist (PDF) and written your risk assessment.
A primary and a secondary proof of identification document that is JP certified or certified by a Service NSW Service Centre.

A statement of training in fireworks use, signed by the current licensed pyrotechnician holder who trained the applicant. This statement must list the fireworks the applicant was trained in (ground display, theatrical/close proximity, and/or Chinese string fireworks).
If an interstate pyrotechnician licence is provided, a certified copy of the front and back of the licence is required.
The type and quantity of fireworks.
The personal and contact details of your assistants.
The type, duration, location, and dates of the display.
Evidence that you have notified all appropriate agencies/parties.

A letter from the relevant local council advising no objections, or a copy of an exclusive use aquatic maritime licence (if the display is on regulated waters and less than seven working days notice is given or for an extended display).
If providing less than 7 days notice to SafeWork NSW, or applying for an extended display, a letter from the local council is also required.

faqs.q: How many fireworks (single use) licences can I apply for?
faqs.a: You can apply for up to 4 FSULs in any 12 months.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a single-use licence and a pyrotechnician's licence?
faqs.a: A single-use licence is only valid for one nominated event. If you plan to use fireworks often or include aerial shell type fireworks, you will need a pyrotechnician's licence.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for this licence?
faqs.a: Applicants must be aged 18 or over, have completed safe use training from a licensed pyrotechnician, and only use the fireworks for an organised public event.
